# Warden

> Warden is a local AI gateway for a team’s configured policies. An administrator describes what to protect, reviews proposed rules and activates them. Warden checks connected AI requests locally before allowed requests continue to the configured model. Free for everyone and open source under Apache-2.0.

- Detailed walkthrough: https://warden-theta.vercel.app/how-it-works
- Source: https://github.com/Wardenlabs/warden
- Downloads and current builds: https://github.com/Wardenlabs/warden/releases/latest
- License: https://github.com/Wardenlabs/warden/blob/main/LICENSE

## Policy and request flow

An administrator can describe a broad policy in one instruction. A capable configured compiler can propose multiple concrete rules, with examples of what should stop and what should pass. Proposed rules are drafts: a person reviews and activates them, individually or as a set. A limited compiler may produce fewer rules; no fixed rule count or generation time is implied.

Active policies apply to requests routed through the appropriate Warden connection. Decisions can allow a request, hold it for human review or block it with a reason. This does not mean every prompt in every application is monitored. The homepage pricing comparison and the detailed walkthrough’s requests, records and step controls are illustrative; they do not run a backend policy check or activate real rules.

Policy evaluation runs locally. Allowed requests can still be sent to the employee’s configured external model. Rule compilation is separate: an administrator may use local inference or a configured compiler endpoint/CLI. Do not describe every inference operation or all AI traffic as local.

## Connections and usage

The page shows Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode. Their appropriate hook or connection must be enabled. Compatible API paths require their own endpoint/key configuration; ordinary unconnected chat or email applications are not implied integrations. Native-client behavior, deadlines and configured failure behavior affect coverage.

Role-based session thresholds use usage reported by connected tools, such as generated tokens and context usage. When reported usage reaches a configured ceiling, the next submitted request is held for administrator review, unless another policy requires a stricter block. This does not interrupt an already-running provider response or independently verify provider billing. Missing usage reporting is not evidence that a session is under budget. Daily request quotas are a separate control.

## Records and privacy

Policy decisions are recorded in an append-only, hash-chained audit log. The audit record stores a prompt hash and decision metadata, not the prompt text; `pnpm run verify-audit` checks the chain and truncation witness.

Masked prompt history is stored separately so an administrator can review what was stopped. Its default retention is seven days and can be changed or disabled. Therefore, “Warden never stores prompt text” is not accurate. See SECURITY.md for retention, redaction and compiler-data details.

## Availability and evidence

Warden is free and licensed under Apache-2.0. The landing links macOS Apple Silicon and Windows x64 installers, with Linux and other builds directed to releases/source. The latest release is the authority for currently published artifacts.

The site and its launch film do not establish universal detection, complete native-client coverage or measured conversion results. Keep current implementation limits and measurements attached to their sources rather than treating historical numbers as a product guarantee.
